title: main reads argv entries as raw float buffers without validating argument count or alignment
reasoning: The executable entrypoint accepts arbitrary CLI invocation but immediately casts argv strings to float and double pointers and reads multiple elements. With no user arguments, line 8 reads from argv[0] as a float buffer; on AArch64 line 14 uses argv[argc-2], which is out of bounds when argc is 1. Even with arguments, argv memory is byte strings, not guaranteed to be suitably sized or aligned for float/double vector loads, so running this as a command can return meaningless results or crash.
reproduction: Build and run the command with no additional arguments on a target where this file compiles; the code will derive src from argv[0] and, on AArch64, src2 from argv[-1].
recommendation: If this is meant to be runnable, validate argc before indexing, parse numeric arguments into properly aligned float/double arrays, and return a clear usage error on invalid input. If this is only a compile-time CPU feature probe, prevent it from being exposed or treated as a user-facing CLI command.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for this feature, and the excerpt shows no defensive path for invalid invocation.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that invokes the built probe with zero and insufficient arguments and asserts a deterministic non-crashing usage error, or add a detection test ensuring compile-only NumPy distutils probes are excluded from CLI feature registration.
minimumFixScope: Limit the change to this probe's entrypoint behavior or to the feature discovery logic that classifies vendored compile checks as runnable commands.
